subject: ela
intro: Good readers can look at two different texts about the same topic and find what is the same AND what is different. This is called comparing and contrasting. We ask: What do both texts say? What does only Text A say? What does only Text B say? This skill helps readers understand a topic more fully by using more than one source.

items.prompt:
Read both passages about frogs.

Text A: 'Frogs are amphibians. They can live on land and in water. Frogs have smooth, wet skin.'

Text B: 'Frogs are cold-blooded animals. They need to be near water to keep their skin moist. Frogs lay their eggs in ponds.'

What is one thing BOTH texts tell us about frogs? What does only Text A tell us?

steps: Read Text A and list what it says: amphibians, live on land and water, smooth wet skin.
Read Text B and list what it says: cold-blooded, need water for moist skin, lay eggs in ponds.
Look for something both texts mention: both say frogs need water or moisture.
What does only Text A say? That frogs are amphibians and have smooth wet skin.
What does only Text B say? That frogs are cold-blooded and lay eggs in ponds.
solution.answer: Both texts tell us that frogs need to be near water. Only Text A tells us that frogs are amphibians and have smooth, wet skin. Only Text B tells us that frogs are cold-blooded and lay their eggs in ponds.

items.prompt:
Read both passages about rain.

Text A: 'Rain falls from clouds. It waters plants and fills rivers and lakes.'

Text B: 'Rain starts as water drops in clouds. When enough drops join together, they fall to the ground as rain.'

What does Text A say about rain that Text B does not? What does Text B explain that Text A does not?

steps: List what Text A says: rain comes from clouds, waters plants, fills rivers and lakes.
List what Text B says: rain starts as water drops in clouds, drops join together, then fall.
Find what only Text A says: that rain waters plants and fills rivers and lakes.
Find what only Text B says: how rain forms (drops joining together).
What is the same: both say rain comes from clouds.
solution.answer: Text A tells us what rain does when it falls: it waters plants and fills rivers and lakes. Text B explains how rain forms inside a cloud. Both texts agree that rain comes from clouds.

items.prompt:
Read both passages about bears.

Text A: 'Bears are large animals. They eat fish, berries, and honey. Bears live in forests.'

Text B: 'Bears sleep through winter. This long sleep is called hibernation. During this time, they live off stored fat.'

Name one similarity and one difference between what the two texts say about bears.

steps: List Text A details: large animals, eat fish/berries/honey, live in forests.
List Text B details: sleep through winter (hibernation), live off stored fat.
Do both texts mention the same thing? Both are about bears, but the specific facts are different.
Similarity: both texts are describing bear behavior and characteristics.
Difference: Text A focuses on what bears eat and where they live; Text B focuses on their winter sleep.
solution.answer: A similarity: both texts describe facts about how bears live. A difference: Text A focuses on what bears eat and where they live, while Text B focuses on bear hibernation in winter.

items.prompt:
Read both passages about the sun.

Text A: 'The sun is a very large star. It gives Earth heat and light. Without the sun, nothing on Earth could live.'

Text B: 'The sun rises in the east every morning and sets in the west every evening. We cannot look directly at the sun because its light is too bright.'

What does Text A focus on? What does Text B focus on?

steps: Text A is about: what the sun is (a star), what it gives us (heat and light), why it matters (life on Earth).
Text B is about: when the sun rises and sets, why we cannot look at it.
Text A focuses on the sun's importance and role.
Text B focuses on how people observe the sun from Earth.
Both texts agree the sun is powerful, but they focus on different aspects.
solution.answer: Text A focuses on the sun's importance to all life on Earth. Text B focuses on how the sun moves across the sky and why it is too bright to look at. Both show the sun is powerful, but from different angles.

items.prompt:
Read both passages about dogs.

Text A: 'Dogs make great pets. They are loyal and love to play. Dogs can be trained to do many things.'

Text B: 'Dogs were first tamed from wolves thousands of years ago. People used dogs to help with hunting and herding animals. Today, dogs help as guide dogs and rescue dogs.'

A student says both texts are saying the same thing: 'dogs are useful.' Do you agree? Explain using details from both texts.

steps: Text A: dogs are loyal pets, love to play, can be trained. Focus: dogs as companions.
Text B: history of dogs, used for hunting/herding, today used as guides and rescuers. Focus: dogs as working animals.
Is the student right that both say dogs are useful?
Text A does say dogs are useful (loyal, trainable) but frames them as companions.
Text B says dogs are useful as workers.
The student is partly right but the texts use the idea of usefulness differently.
solution.answer: The student is partly right. Both texts show dogs are useful. But Text A focuses on dogs as loyal companions and pets, while Text B focuses on dogs as working animals with a long history. The idea of usefulness is shared, but what kind of usefulness is different.

items.prompt:
Read both passages about butterflies.

Text A: 'Butterflies have four wings covered in tiny scales. Their wings are often bright and colorful.'

Text B: 'Butterflies go through four stages of life: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, and butterfly. This is called metamorphosis.'

What does Text A tell us about butterflies? What does Text B tell us? What is different about their focus?
items.hint: Think about whether each text describes what butterflies look like or what butterflies do and how they change.

steps: Text A: describes the wings (four, covered in scales, colorful). Focus: appearance.
Text B: describes the life cycle (four stages, metamorphosis). Focus: life stages/change.
Are these the same focus? No: Text A is about appearance; Text B is about development.
What is different: Text A tells us what butterflies look like; Text B tells us how they grow.
solution.answer: Text A focuses on what butterflies look like (their colorful, scale-covered wings). Text B focuses on how butterflies grow and change through four life stages. The texts are different because one covers appearance and the other covers life cycle.

items.prompt:
Read both passages about snow.

Text A: 'Snow is frozen water that falls from clouds. Each snowflake has a unique shape with six sides.'

Text B: 'Snow covers the ground in winter and keeps plant roots warm. Animals like rabbits and foxes change the color of their fur to match the snow.'

Name one fact found in BOTH texts and one fact found only in Text B.
items.hint: Read each text carefully and look for what they share and what is different.

steps: Text A says: snow is frozen water, snowflakes have six sides.
Text B says: snow covers ground in winter, keeps plant roots warm, animals change fur color.
Is there anything both texts mention? Both mention that snow comes in winter (Text B says 'winter' directly, Text A implies it by talking about snow falling).
Something only in Text B: animals change fur color to match the snow.
Something only in Text A: snowflakes have six sides and unique shapes.
solution.answer: A fact in both texts: snow relates to cold/winter conditions. A fact only in Text B: animals like rabbits and foxes change the color of their fur to match the snow.

items.prompt:
Read both passages about community helpers.

Text A: 'Police officers keep neighborhoods safe. They patrol streets and help people in trouble.'

Text B: 'Firefighters keep people safe from fires. They also help in car accidents and medical emergencies.'

How are the two community helpers alike? How are they different?
items.hint: Think about what they both do (keeping people safe) and what is different about each job.

steps: Text A: police officers keep neighborhoods safe, patrol streets, help people in trouble.
Text B: firefighters keep people safe from fires, help in car accidents and emergencies.
What is alike: both community helpers keep people safe.
What is different: police officers patrol streets; firefighters deal with fires and emergencies.
Different jobs, same general goal: keeping people safe.
solution.answer: Both police officers and firefighters keep people safe. They are different because police officers patrol streets and help people in trouble, while firefighters handle fires, car accidents, and medical emergencies.

items.prompt:
Read both passages about plants needing sunlight.

Text A: 'Plants need sunlight to make their food. They use sunlight, water, and air to grow.'

Text B: 'Some plants can grow in shady places with very little sunlight. Ferns and moss grow well under trees where the sun does not reach.'

Do these two texts agree or disagree? Explain using details from both.
items.hint: Text A makes a general statement. Does Text B give a different view or add to it?

steps: Text A says plants need sunlight to make food and grow.
Text B says some plants grow in shade with little sunlight. Examples: ferns and moss.
Do they disagree? Text A says sunlight is needed; Text B says some plants need very little.
They are partly different: Text A gives the general rule; Text B shows an exception.
Together they give a fuller picture: most plants need sun, but some can thrive in shade.
solution.answer: The texts partly agree and partly show different ideas. Text A says plants need sunlight to grow. Text B shows that some plants like ferns and moss can grow in shady places with little sunlight. Together they show that the need for sunlight varies by type of plant.

items.prompt:
Read both passages about oceans.

Text A: 'The ocean covers more than half of the Earth. It is home to millions of animals, from tiny fish to giant whales.'

Text B: 'The ocean provides food for people around the world. Fishermen catch fish, shrimp, and crabs from the sea every day.'

What is one idea both texts share? What is one idea only Text B discusses?
items.hint: Both texts are about the ocean. Look for what they both agree on, then find what only Text B adds.

steps: Text A: ocean covers half of Earth, home to millions of animals.
Text B: ocean provides food for people, fishermen catch fish/shrimp/crabs.
What do both share? Both are about the ocean and what it contains.
Both agree: the ocean has living things in it.
Only Text B: the ocean is a source of food for people.
solution.answer: Both texts share the idea that the ocean contains many living things. Only Text B discusses how people use the ocean to get food by fishing for fish, shrimp, and crabs.
